events.title: FBI Flying Discs Case File 62-HQ-83894
events.summary: 21-year, 18-section investigative archive on UFOs and flying discs. Includes Oak Ridge TN photo evidence, propulsion proposals, eyewitness testimonies, and conventions. Many sections newly declassified with fewer redactions than the FBI Vault version.

crossRefs.note: Section 2 photo evidence and security-officer sightings 1947–50

events.title: SHAEF Foo Fighters & Night Phenomena
events.summary: SHAEF messages on "night phenomena (foofighters)," flak rockets, unidentified cylindrical objects, and blinking lights. Repeated references to observations by the 415th Night Fighter Squadron over Germany.

events.title: Krasuski — German Compound Sighting (1944)
events.summary: FBI 1957 interview report (recounting a 1944 event). Krasuski described seeing a large, circular, vertically-rising vehicle near a German military compound during WWII.

events.title: Air Materiel Command — Flying Disc Concern
events.summary: Memorandums establishing flying disc/saucer sightings as a formal matter of concern for the Air Materiel Command — six months after Roswell.

events.title: 1948 Flying Disc Investigations
events.summary: Memorandums and forms governing how military personnel were to report flying disc sightings — the year of Project Sign.

events.title: Netherlands Air Force Intel Report
events.summary: Air Force intelligence report from November 1948 on UFOs and flying saucers observed over the Netherlands.

events.title: 1949 Flying Disc Incident Reports
events.summary: UFO incident reports filed under 1948 Flight Service Regulation 200-4. Includes military and Civilian Aviation Authority witnesses, MATS/AACS messages, diagrams, and a Japan weather station report.

events.title: Project Blue Book–era Incident Summaries (#1–233)
events.summary: 233 standardized "Check-List - Unidentified Flying Objects" incident summaries with witness lists, statements, and narrative descriptions — the working files behind Project Blue Book era investigations.

events.title: State Dept. Memo on Increased UFO Reports
events.summary: 1952 State Department memo on the surge in UFO reports — possible explanations include technological progress, USAF opinions, and historical sighting records. Filed during the famous 1952 Washington flap.

events.title: USSR Trans-Caucasus Sighting
events.summary: USAF Air Intelligence Information Report on an eyewitness account of an unconventional aircraft ascending and flying through the trans-Caucasus region of the USSR — rare Cold War cross-border UFO intelligence.

events.title: Detroit FBI UFO Memo
events.summary: FBI memo: a Detroit man described a "circular object with a crystal-type dome." Bureau recommended forwarding to "proper air force authorities."

events.title: Presidential Memo on the "Space Alien Race Question"
events.summary: Memo from the Executive Office of the President / National Aeronautics and Space Council on plans if alien intelligence is discovered, the possibility of life on Mars, and diplomatic policy. One of the most striking documents in the release.

events.title: Gemini VII — Borman & Lovell Observe a "Bogey"
events.summary: Frank Borman radios Houston: an unidentified "bogey" with a debris field of "trillions of particles." Lovell describes a "brilliant body in the sun against a black background." Handwritten margin note: "UFO Sighting by Borman."

events.title: Apollo 11 — Aldrin's Lights & Object
events.summary: Apollo 11 Technical Crew Debriefing — Buzz Aldrin describes three observations: a sizable object on the way to the Moon, repeated flashes of light inside the cabin while trying to sleep, and a bright light source on the return trip tentatively assumed to be a laser.

events.title: Apollo 12 — Bean's Particles & Conrad's Debris
events.summary: Astronaut Alan Bean describes particles and flashes of light "sailing off in space" through the Alignment Optical Telescope, "escaping the Moon." Mission Commander Pete Conrad observes floating debris illuminated by the lunar module tracking light. Five archival photos (VM1–VM5) highlight phenomena above the lunar horizon.

events.title: Apollo 17 — Triangular Lights & ACTIVE DOW Investigation
events.summary: The headline NASA case. Image NASA-UAP-VM6 shows three "dots" in a triangular formation in the lunar sky. DOW has opened an active case under PURSUE — preliminary US government analysis suggests a physical object in the scene, and the original film has been obtained for full NASA/DOW analysis. Cernan reported intense flashing lights "imposing" themselves between his eyes; Schmitt reported a flash on the lunar surface north of crater Grimaldi.

events.title: Skylab Crews — Light Flashes & Red Satellite
events.summary: All three Skylab crews reported light-flash phenomena. Skylab 3 reported a "rather large red star" — an object brighter than Jupiter that they tracked for 5–10 minutes, "obviously a satellite in a very similar orbit to our own." Skylab 4 saw lights flashing outside with definite relative motion.

events.title: COMETA — "UFOs and Defense: What Should We Prepare For?"
events.summary: 94-page briefing package: full English COMETA Report (originally VSD magazine, France, July 1999), authored by retired French generals, admirals, and aerospace scientists with foreword by André Lebeau (former CNES chairman). Hand-delivered to Washington in April 2001 by Carol Rosin (former von Braun spokesperson, founder of the Institute for Security and Cooperation in Outer Space) and her husband, actor Jon Cypher. Includes John Callahan's FAA testimony on JAL 1628 and Enrique Kolbeck's Mexico City ATC radar evidence. Filed under NASA in this release — itself revealing.

events.title: Papua New Guinea — High-Speed Aircraft
events.summary: US Embassy Port Moresby cabled INDOPACOM after PNG intelligence reported "fast-moving objects with lights, contrails, and noise" the night of Jan 24, 1985. Air Niugini pilot's radar "picked up aircraft flying south to north at high altitude and high speed." Locals were "frightened by overflights." Embassy implicitly asking: were these ours? Implicit answer: no.

events.title: Tajik 747 Encounter Over Kazakhstan
events.summary: A Tajik pilot and three American citizens flying a 747 at 41,000 feet encountered a UAP: bright light of "enormous intensity" approaching at extreme speed and far higher altitude. Photographs reportedly captured 90-degree turns, corkscrew maneuvers, "bullet-in-flight" appearance. Contrails estimated at 100,000 feet — "too high to leave contrails by ordinary aircraft."

events.title: Russia Blames UFOs for Kodori Gorge Bombing
events.summary: Georgian Foreign Ministry alleged Russian aircraft violated Georgian airspace and bombed parts of the Kodori Gorge on Oct 28–29, 2001. Russia denied involvement and suggested it could have been UFOs. Cable authors note Russians "typically engage in the 'bold lie' when they wish to conceal actions." UFOs as state-craft cover story.

events.title: Mexican Congress: Aerial Space Protection Law
events.summary: State Department cable on Mexican Congress hearing testimony on UAP — discussion of an "Aerial Space Protection Law" that, if approved, would make Mexico the first country to formally acknowledge alien presence on Earth. Witnesses presented two alleged alien corpses and videos of Mexican pilots' encounters. Disagreement on the corpses' authenticity.

events.title: Turkmenistan UFOlogists as Civil Society Partners
events.summary: A wry note from US Embassy Ashgabat: in tightly-controlled Turkmenistan, the local UFOlogist community had emerged as a "reliable partner" for civil-society building, "to the bemusement of the cable's author," because "everyone in Turkmenistan, apparently, is interested in UFOs."

events.title: Latakia, Syria — P-8A Sea-Skim Tracking
events.summary: A US Navy P-8A pilot tracked an object via EO/IR sensor in apparent "sea skim mode," ~500 knots (575 mph) southeasterly. P-8A lost visual contact after two minutes.

events.title: Middle East — Erratic White Object Over Water
events.summary: Navy Range Fouler debrief plus 2 min 17 sec infrared video. A "solid white object" flew through the field of view making "erratic [movements] above the water." Sensor cycled contrast filters and zoom levels but never achieved a tracking lock.

events.title: Arabian Gulf — 2020 Cluster (10+ Reports)
events.summary: Sustained cluster of UAP encounters reported by US CENTCOM operators throughout 2020. Multiple speeds (278–321 knots), multiple shapes (line of dots, balloon-like, formations). Range Fouler reports describe wing/airframe structures and abrupt directional changes. CENTCOM submissions dominate the 2020 set.

events.title: Southern US — Air Force Sighting (PR-45)
events.summary: USAF report. Operator observed "several bright objects maneuvering quickly west to east northeast." Onboard targeting pod tracked a UAP for ~20 seconds before it "dimmed and disappeared."

events.title: Gulf of Aden — 8-Minute IR Track
events.summary: A "round, cold object" tracked for 8 minutes via "black hot" IR sensor. UAP traveled at 277 mph with abrupt directional changes during the encounter.

events.title: Iraq, May 2022 — 5 UAP Cross Screen (PR-19)
events.summary: 5-second IR video. CENTCOM operator reported observing "5x UAP fly across the screen" — one assessed as a "possible missile," remaining four as "possible birds."

events.title: Kuwait — Operator-Annotated Image (PR-20)
events.summary: Still image submitted with the original reporter's red-line circle around an "elongated area of contrast." Operator unable to positively identify.

events.title: Iraq — "Probable SU-27/35" (PR-21)
events.summary: 10-second IR video showing two areas of contrast moving together. Mission report describes them as a "probable SU-27/35" — Russian Federation aircraft. AARO inserts a comment confirming SU-27/35 designation.

events.title: Syria — North-South Track (PR-22)
events.summary: 14-second dual IR/EO video, single UAP "moving from north to south," duration under one minute.

events.title: Iraq, Dec 2022 — West-to-East (PR-23)
events.summary: 10-second IR video. "Possible UAP" flying west to east; observer did not pursue.

events.title: "Possible Balloon" at 2,100 ft, Syria
events.summary: A "possible balloon" observed at approximately 2,100 feet — context: shortly after the Chinese spy balloon incident over CONUS.

events.title: Western US — 7 Federal Witness Cluster
events.summary: AARO summary: SEVEN federal-employee witnesses separately reported four phenomena over two days: (1) "orbs launching other orbs" at distance, (2) a large stationary glowing orb at close range, (3) pursuing a large near-ground phenomenon, (4) a "translucent kite-like" phenomenon. AARO calls this "among the most compelling within AARO's current holdings" — the strongest endorsement language in Release 01.

events.title: Ellipsoid Bronze Object — Composite Sketch + 3 FBI 302s
events.summary: FBI Lab composite sketch overlaid on a real site photo. Corroborating eyewitness accounts: an "ellipsoid bronze metallic object" 130–195 feet long, "materializing out of a bright light in the sky" and "disappearing instantaneously." Three FBI 302 interview reports describe the object as "metallic bronze," "metallic/gray," and a "bright light over the horizon." Among the most concrete and corroborated cases in the entire release.

events.title: UAE, October 2023 — Two Long Tracks (PR-26, PR-27)
events.summary: Two CENTCOM video releases tied to D23: 43 seconds and 4 minutes 57 seconds of IR footage tracking areas of contrast through extended sensor maneuvering. Among the longest video releases in the tranche.

events.title: Greece, Oct 2023 — Sea-Skimming "90° Turns" (PR-34, PR-35)
events.summary: Two reports two days apart. PR-34: UAP "flying just above the surface of the ocean," making "multiple 90-degree turns at an estimated 80 mph." PR-35: UAP "flying straight above the ocean towards land." 2 min 57 sec IR video shows the sensor tracking through reticle locks, contrast filters, and zoom cycles before losing it against the background.

events.title: "Bouncy Ball" — 7-Min Track at 424 Knots, Syria
events.summary: UAP "shaped as a bouncy ball" tracked consistently at ~424 knots (483 mph) for at least 7 minutes. Operator assessed as "benign."

events.title: INDOPACOM 2023 — Three Co-Moving Objects
events.summary: INDOPACOM submitted 1 min 59 sec of IR video showing three distinct areas of contrast that "appeared to maintain a fixed position and orientation relative to one another."

events.title: Greece, Jan 2024 — Diamond on SWIR ONLY (PR-28)
events.summary: Striking technical case. Diamond-shaped UAP with a non-maneuvering probe at the bottom, traveling ~434 knots (499 mph) — visible ONLY through Short-Wave Infrared (SWIR), invisible to visible spectrum and standard IR. Operator switched modalities live during the 2-minute encounter and lost the object when leaving SWIR.

events.title: INDOPACOM 2024 — "Football-Shaped Body" (PR-46)
events.summary: 9-second IR video. Football-shaped body with three radial projections — one vertical, two angled at 45 degrees from the major axis. The most morphologically distinctive object in Release 01.

events.title: UAE, June 2024 — Inverted Teardrop (PR-29)
events.summary: NORTHCOM submission. 21 seconds of IR video showing an inverted-teardrop area of contrast with a vertically linear trailing mass. Observer noted possible reflection from object in water; operator estimated 24,000 ft, 163 knots.

events.title: Gulf of Aden, Jul 2024 — "Faster than Flying Speed"
events.summary: UAP maintaining a "straight flight path at same altitude," with speed "faster than flying speed." Operator followed "till the distance became too far."

events.title: Iraq — Lens Flare Post-Missile Launch
events.summary: During an AGM-176 Griffin missile weapons calibration test, MX-20/MX-25 IR sensors caught a lens flare from a UAP moving "at a high rate of speed." Reporter assessed "a significant heat source."

events.title: Syria, Oct 2024 — "Halo Effect" Cluster (PR-31, 32, 33)
events.summary: Same-day cluster of three FMV camera observations. Operator reported "misshapen and uneven ball of white light" with multiple "glares or light" from "unknown origin," and a "light/glare halo effect" at the top of the FMV feed.

events.title: Djibouti / Africa 2025 (PR-43)
events.summary: AFRICOM submission. 2 seconds of IR footage showing a small, barely distinguishable area of contrast crossing the field of view. The video is looped for viewing purposes.

events.title: INDOPACOM April 2025 — Email Correspondence
events.summary: Email correspondence describing the content of an INDOPACOM mission report and requesting clarification.

events.title: FBI 2025 Photo Series — A1–A8 + B1–B24 (32 stills)
events.summary: 32 monochrome still images from US government systems with crosshair reticles. Set A: location not provided. Set B: Western US, system date/time incorrect at capture. Each shows small dark or light objects against grainy or mountainous backgrounds. A6: object centered exactly in the reticle. B6: structured object with appendage. B7: helicopter alongside a small dark object below. Operators "unable to positively identify" any of them.

events.title: USPER — "Super-Hot Orb" at US Military Facility
events.summary: FBI 302 interview with a SENIOR US INTELLIGENCE OFFICIAL. After helicopter searches at a US military facility, found a "super-hot" orb hovering over the ground. The orb "travelled for 20 miles at a speed too fast for the helicopter in pursuit." A "swarm" of lights was seen moving in all directions, then 4–5 additional orbs flaring up and down across the area for 30 minutes. First-hand testimony from a senior intelligence officer is exceptional within Release 01.

events.title: Department of the Army 2026 (PR-49)
events.summary: 1 minute 49 seconds of IR video. Sensor tracks an initial area of interest, then disengages and pans to track TWO areas of contrast. The most recent UAP video in Release 01.

events.title: PURSUE Release 01 — Public Disclosure
events.summary: Cleared for public release: 162 records (120 PDFs, 28 videos, 14 images, 4,185 PDF pages, 2.3 GB total) hosted at war.gov/UFO. Interagency effort: White House, ODNI (Tulsi Gabbard), DOE, AARO, NASA (Jared Isaacman), FBI (Kash Patel), Department of War (Pete Hegseth). Rolling tranches every few weeks. All cases marked UNRESOLVED.

events.title: CIA-UAP-D001, Intelligence Information Report, USSR, 1973
events.summary: Declassified CIA intelligence information report covering a Soviet-era UAP-relevant case (December 20, 1973). Released in Release 02 alongside the DOE, DOW, and ODNI documents.

events.title: DOE-UAP-D001, Enhanced PANTEX Imagery
events.summary: Declassified DOE imagery from the Pantex Plant (Department of Energy weapons assembly/disassembly facility, Texas). Sensor of record: Ground Surveillance Radar Tower ENE; Sandia National Labs enhanced the returns. One of the few archive records where primary-source sensor data is connected to a documented theoretical physics framework (DIA AAWSA, 2010).

events.title: DOE-UAP-D002, James Tuck Correspondence, 1970s

events.title: DOE-UAP-D003, Pajarito Astronomers Invitation, 1986
events.summary: Declassified invitation/report concerning astronomers' observations from the Pajarito Plateau, Los Alamos area, May 20 1986. Part of Release 02.

events.title: DOW-UAP-D017, UAP Reported at Sandia Base, 1948-1950
events.summary: Department of War general correspondence concerning UAP reports at Sandia Base, 1948-1950. Largest single PDF in Release 02 (~67 MB).

events.title: DOW-UAP-PR050 — 4 UAP Formation Iran 26 Aug 2022 over water [CALLSIGN]
events.summary:
On March 6, 2026, eight members of the U.S. House of Representatives requested access to 51 potentially UAP-related records allegedly held by the Department of War and the Intelligence Community. The All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) identified a collection of responsive materials held on a classified network. Many of these materials lack a substantiated chain-of-custody.

AARO assesses that this video, whose uploader-defined title is, “4 UAP Formation Iran 26 Aug 2022 over water [CALLSIGN],” is likely derived from an infrared sensor aboard a U.S. military platform operating within the United States Central Command area of responsibility in 2022. A user uploaded this video to a classified network in June 2024.

Video Description:

00:05-00:06: An area of contrast enters the sensor field-of-view from the top left corner of the screen.

This video description is provided for informational purposes only. Readers should not interpret any part of this description as reflecting an analytical judgment, investigative conclusion, or factual determination regarding the described event’s validity, nature, or significance.

events.title: NASA-UAP-D005 — Apollo 17 Crew Debriefing for Science, 1973
events.summary:
Apollo 17 was the ninth crewed U.S. mission to the Moon, and the sixth to land Astronauts on the lunar surface. This document is an excerpt from the Apollo 17 Crew Debriefing for Science on January 8, 1973, in which Dick Henry, co-investigator on the ultraviolet experiment on Apollo 17, discusses seeing results that were unexpected. 
•	Pages 119-120. “One of the most exciting results of X-ray astronomy was the fact that an X-ray background was observed over the sky that nobody had expected, and part of this is the gamma-ray background that Dr. Trombka talked about. In the UV, nobody knows, but you never know until you look. You do have to deal with this background of stars that we know is there. So, we did look at a large number of different points at high galactic latitudes, both north and south. The spectrum that we see is above this dark count. In other words, this abnormally high dark current did not, in fact, interfere with that experiment. The spectrum that we see looks like the spectrum of the hot star; however, we know that there were no hot stars within our field of view. Therefore, the most conservative interpretation, I think, is that what we're seeing is light from hot stars in the galactic plane going up out of the plane and reflecting off interstellar dust. There are certain characteristics of the spectrum, though, that don't fit that theory, and it's at least possible that this is extragalactic radiation. I'm looking forward very much to the detailed computer study of this, but it's going to take a long time.”

I had one which I thought was a flash on the lunar surface. That one period of time when we had the blindfolds on for the ALFMED [Apollo Light Flash Moving Emulsion Detector] experiment there were just no visible flashes, although that evening, that night, before I went to sleep, I noticed that I was seeing the light flashes again.”

events.title: DOE-UAP-D004, Los Alamos Conference on Aerial Phenomena, 1949
events.summary: This document is a transcript of a 1949 conference held at Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory (now Los Alamos National Laboratory), Los Alamos, New Mexico. Attendees included several eminent scientists and physicists, many of whom had contributed to the development of the first nuclear weapons during the Manhattan Project. The purpose of the conference was to discuss and gather hypotheses to account for the nature and origin of a phenomenon involving “green fireballs” that had been reported over a period of several months in the vicinity of the laboratory. The group did not come to a consensus on a likely attribution for the phenomenon, though a leading hypothesis was that the observations may have been related to meteors entering the atmosphere at a shallow angle and high altitude. Dr. Edward Teller suggested that if not a “material body,” an “electron phenomenon” might be the cause, while Dr. Lincoln LaPaz, an expert specializing in meteorics, expressed that “nothing like this, to [his] knowledge, has ever been observed in the case of meteorite drops.”

events.title: DOW-UAP-D094, Analysis of Flying Object Incidents in the United States, 1949

The analysis includes an assessment of various reported unidentified flying object (UFO) incidents and theories to account for their nature and origin. Overall, the study assesses that “it appears that some object has been seen; however, the identification of that object cannot be readily accomplished.” The study offers that two “reasonable” origins might account for the phenomena: technologies of a domestic or foreign origin. It also suggests that, if foreign, it is prudent for the United States to assume that UFO observations are attributable to scientific, military, or intelligence activities of the Soviet Union, and, in that case, to take seriously the threat such objects may pose. The file also contains selected contemporary UFO reports and examples of experimental “flying wing” type aircraft planforms that might account for certain commonly reported UFO characteristics. AARO Comment: This file appears to be a later revision of the file contained in DOW-UAP-D093, whose content is substantively similar.

events.title: CIA-UAP-D020, Memorandum on Unconventional Aircraft Sightings, 1955
events.summary: This memorandum summarizes a Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) debriefing of a group of four individuals who reported observing a “flying saucer” or “unconventional aircraft” in 1955. The group, which included U.S. Senator Richard Russell, a U.S. military service member, and two U.S. Government officials, reported observing a luminescent “greenish-yellow” phenomenon, as seen from aboard a train while traveling within the Soviet Union, in present-day Azerbaijan, between Baku and Tiflis (Tbilisi, Georgia). events.title: DOW-UAP-D092, Department of the Air Force Committee to Review Project Bluebook, 1966-1967
events.summary: This file documents the 1966-1967 deliberations and recommendations of the U.S. Air Force (USAF) Scientific Advisory Board’s Ad Hoc Committee to Review Project Blue Book. Project Blue Book was a 1952-1969 USAF program to investigate the nature and origin of unidentified flying objects (UFO). The Committee recommended that the USAF contract a scientific team composed of university-affiliated representatives to investigate selected UFO sightings. The USAF subsequently adopted the Committee’s recommendation.

events.title: DOW-UAP-D093, Analysis of Flying Object Incidents in the United States, 1948
events.summary: This file contains a U.S. Air Force (USAF) Air Intelligence Division study, “Analysis of Flying Object Incidents in the United States,” Study No. 203, dated 12/10/1948. The analysis includes an assessment of various reported unidentified flying object (UFO) incidents and theories to account for their nature and origin. Overall, the study assesses that “it appears that some object has been seen; however, the identification of that object cannot be readily accomplished.” The study offers that two “reasonable” origins might account for the phenomena: technologies of a domestic or foreign origin. It also suggests that, if foreign, it is prudent for the United States to assume that UFO observations are attributable to scientific, military, or intelligence activities of the Soviet Union, and, in that case, to take seriously the threat such objects may pose. The file also contains contemporary UFO reports and examples of experimental “flying wing” type aircraft planforms that might account for certain commonly reported UFO characteristics. AARO Comment: This file appears to be an earlier draft version of the file contained in DOW-UAP-D094, whose content is substantively similar.

events.title: DOW-UAP-D095, Joint U.S.-Canadian Aviation Projects and UFO Sighting Reports, 1954-1955
events.summary: This file contains reports, memoranda, and correspondence concerning various then-developmental vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) aircraft. The file includes assessments of the experimental potential of the “Avro Project Y2,” a joint U.S.-Canadian near-circular VTOL aircraft that is similar in appearance to contemporary popular descriptions of unidentified flying objects (UFO). A 1954 memorandum opines that VTOL aircraft with a circular planform may be mistaken for UFOs to observers unfamiliar with such technologies. It also recommends that UFO reports in the vicinity of Soviet military operations or assets be re-examined to assess whether they may be attributable to previously unknown advanced VTOL aircraft of foreign design. The file also contains correspondence relating to a UFO incident involving a U.S. Air Force (USAF) KC-97 flying near Newfoundland, Canada in July 1955. A USAF committee found that the characteristics described in the report were inconsistent with those of known Soviet, American, or Canadian military systems. The committee was also “unable to explain the simultaneous ground radar returns and aircrew visual sightings.” It also contains correspondence relating to the potential value of data from incidental radar collection of meteors entering the atmosphere. USAF Air Research and Development Command recommended using that data to improve the performance of the AN/FPS-17 radar system. Finally, the file contains correspondence indicating support for the Communications Instructions for Reporting Vital Intelligence Sightings (CIRVIS) program, a joint U.S.-Canadian civil-military program to standardize reporting methods for unusual or unidentified airborne and maritime hazards and threats.

events.title: NASA-UAP-D026, Apollo 14 Debriefing, 1971
events.summary: This file contains segment 1 of 2 of the Apollo 14 post-mission crew debriefing at the Manned Spacecraft Center (now Johnson Space Center), Houston, Texas. In the recording, crew members and debriefers discuss the “light flash phenomena,” a then novel, now well-documented biological effect where high-energy cosmic rays pass through the eye and strike the retina, causing the perception of light streaks or flashes. The questioners attempt to distinguish the characteristics of the observed phenomena. The debriefing continues in the next file (NASA-UAP-D027), which contains some overlapping audio content.
